One-line judgment: a cashier is not just someone who scans an item and takes money and gives change; the role completes a transaction that is verifiable, traceable and clearly accounted for at cashier positions in retail and other non-financial establishments — receiving payment by cash, cheque, bank card, mobile payment and vouchers, checking items, prices, promotions and tax amounts, issuing receipts and handling refunds and change, counting the starting till and reconciling the total transaction amount, preparing shift reconciliations and non-monetary records, keeping the checkout area tidy and restocked, and handling and escalating customer complaints and abnormal transactions according to institutional rules. O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2 (little or no preparation to some preparation, SVP below 6.0), with an interest code of CE (Conventional, Enterprising), and the occupation page marks Bright Outlook. The core boundary is that cashiers are usually not a uniformly licensed occupation, but refund and discount authorization and final transaction determination are usually decided by institutional rules and authorization; where age-restricted purchases by minors, food safety and premises hygiene, cash and voucher management, and customer and payment information protection are involved, separate requirements apply under the applicable jurisdiction and institutional procedures; the output of this occupation is accurate transactions with traceable vouchers and reconciliation records, and it does not replace the determination of refunds, discrepancies and compliance matters by operator, compliance and finance positions.

Signals to keep exploring: you can keep pricing and change accurate under continuous customer flow and long periods of standing, and are willing to check and document every refund and discount according to the rules (the O*NET work context shows 96% are in contact with others continuously, 79% have face-to-face discussions every day, 78% have telephone conversations every day, 67% make decisions every day, 51% stand continuously or almost continuously, 46% continuously handle and control objects and tools by hand, 27% consider repeating the same tasks extremely important and 26% very important), you can handle dissatisfied customers or checkout and payment failures through the process instead of relaxing the rules yourself, and you are willing to reconcile cash and transaction discrepancies at shift handover and report them truthfully.

Conditions for pausing high investment first: you have not yet completed a full closed-loop exercise that runs from counting the starting till at the beginning of a shift, checking out and verifying prices and promotions, handling refunds and change, to reconciling and handing over at the end of the shift; or you are unwilling to check prices, promotions and payment results transaction by transaction, unwilling to follow the rules on refund and discount authorization, unwilling to escalate through the process when a customer is dissatisfied or equipment fails and instead just get through it; and do not treat having helped out at a convenience store as proof that you already have cash reconciliation, refund authorization, age and food safety verification and discrepancy handling ability.

Education, qualifications and authorization must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2 (little or no preparation to some preparation, SVP below 6.0), and the education survey shows 44% of respondents think a high school diploma or equivalent is needed, 37% think less than a high school diploma is enough and 9% think a postsecondary education certificate is needed; the occupation page lists no national certification and no registered apprenticeship position titles approved by the U.S. Department of Labor, which shows that the entry threshold for this occupation comes mainly from on-the-job training and institutional rules, not industry certification. In the United States, cashiers are usually not a uniformly licensed occupation, but positions involving the sale of age-restricted goods such as alcohol and tobacco, food safety and premises hygiene, and cash and voucher management have separate requirements under state and local regulations and institutional rules; in Chinese mainland, the related duties may fall within retail, food service and store service positions, subject to the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, and public rules on food safety and premises hygiene. Education and training, industry certification, statutory qualifications and practice eligibility, job hiring and authorization, and authority over refunds, discounts and discrepancy determinations are five different things.

One line: this is a position that turns how much was collected on this transaction, how much change is owed, why a refund was given, to whom it was given and whether the books balance into verifiable evidence, producing correct payment, change and payment vouchers, receipts and refund vouchers, shift till and reconciliation records, anomaly and discrepancy records, and customer service and complaint handling records; it is not a pricing, promotion and merchandise decision role, and it does not replace the determination of refund authority, discrepancy handling and compliance matters by operator, finance and compliance positions. U.S. wages use a public statistical framing, and this route obtained no occupational-level statistical framing for Chinese mainland, so this page shows the gap rather than filling in a proxy figure.

The work of this occupation can be divided into three categories: first, checkout and settlement (receiving payment by cash, cheque, bank card, mobile payment and vouchers, using scanning equipment and cash registers to check items, prices, promotions and tax amounts, totalling bills, issuing receipts and giving change, and weighing and pricing items sold by weight); second, customer service and exception handling (greeting and directing customers, answering questions about products, processes and policies, helping customers find items, handling returns and exchanges, receiving and resolving complaints, and handling refunds and discounts within the authorized scope while escalating matters beyond that authority); third, reconciliation and shift handover (counting the starting till at the start of the shift, calculating and recording the total transaction amount, checking amounts received against total sales, preparing non-monetary reports and records, counting and bundling cash, keeping the checkout area tidy and restocked, and completing handover). All three share one chain built around correct and traceable amounts, complete vouchers and clear accountability.
Checkout and settlement

Check items, prices, promotions and tax amounts → receive cash, bank card, mobile payment or vouchers → total the bill and calculate the change owed → issue receipts and payment vouchers → weigh and price items sold by weight and double-check → produce a complete and traceable transaction record
Customer service and exception handling

Greet and direct customers → answer questions about products, processes and policies → help customers find where items are → receive returns, exchanges and complaints and judge authority according to the rules → handle refunds and discounts within the authorized scope and document them → escalate disputes beyond your authority or involving fraud and safety to the shift lead or supervisor

Count the starting till at the start of the shift and confirm the amount and change → record each transaction and check amounts received against total sales → count and bundle cash and prepare the balance sheet and shift reconciliation → record discrepancies and anomalies with the handling and escalation path → keep the checkout area tidy and restocked and complete handover → write out open items and follow-ups clearly

Cashiers centre on receiving and paying out for transactions at non-financial institutions, vouchers and reconciliation; retail promotion, rental deposits, customer service tickets, bank account business and inventory each have different objects. Some adjacent positions may also take payment or process refunds, so it is not correct to say uniformly that customer service does not handle cash; transfers must check the target duties and authorization, and names cannot simply be swapped.
Core purpose

Make every transaction meet the requirements of correct amount, verifiable receipt and payment, and traceable vouchers: check transaction by transaction so the amount matches the items and prices, use vouchers and records so transactions can be questioned later, and use shift reconciliation and discrepancy reporting so problems are not carried past the accounting and customer relationship.
Main objects and basis

The objects are goods, services and admission prices, cash, coins, cheques, bank cards, mobile payments, vouchers and coupons, cash registers, scanning equipment, weighing equipment and payment terminals, receipts, refund vouchers and shift reconciliation sheets, and customer enquiries, complaints and return or exchange requests; the people you work with include customers, the shift lead or supervisor, finance and loss prevention positions, merchandise and inventory positions, and equipment and payment service providers. The basis is the institution's price, promotion and discount rules, its payment, refund and voucher management rules, its cash, voucher and till management system, age-restricted purchase limits and food safety and premises hygiene requirements, and the statutory requirements and institutional procedures for protecting customer and payment information.
Core process

Counting the starting till, scanning and checking items and prices, receiving and verifying payment, calculating and double-checking change, issuing receipts and vouchers, receiving returns, exchanges and complaints, handling refunds and discounts according to authorization, recording transactions and anomalies, shift reconciliation and discrepancy reporting, and cleaning, restocking and handover.
Main outputs

Accurate payment, change and payment vouchers, receipts, refund vouchers and redemption records, weight-pricing and bill totalling records, shift till counts and reconciliation records, balance sheets and non-monetary reports of transaction amounts and counts, anomaly and discrepancy records and escalation records, and customer service, complaint handling and handover records.
Responsible party

You price, take payment, give change, record and reconcile according to your job duties; pricing, refund exceptions, discrepancy investigation and compliance matters are allocated by the actual store rules, and it is not assumed that every store has finance and compliance positions. Operators and staff must still perform applicable obligations such as information protection, and not push all compliance responsibility onto management positions. If the amount or payment result is in doubt, pause the relevant transactions you are handling and report, rather than balancing the books yourself or taking payment twice.
Access and licensing

Equipment, till, refund, discount and reversal authority are checked against the actual position, and statutory qualifications, age verification, food conditions and information handling are confirmed separately; training records and internal authorization do not replace legal conditions. The U.S. FDA Tobacco21 rule provides that tobacco must not be sold to anyone under 21, and since 2024-09-30 purchasers under 30 of cigarettes, smokeless tobacco and covered tobacco products must have their age verified with photo identification; this is not only a state and local rule. Alcohol, food positions and other local licensing conditions were not checked state by state this round, and institutional training does not automatically create a licence. Article 24 of China's Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests concerns returns, exchanges and repairs for quality non-conformity, while the seven-day no-reason return in Article 25 applies to online, television, telephone and mail-order sales and has exceptions, and is not applied uniformly to all in-store transactions; store rules must not exclude statutory rights. Article 59 of the Law on the Protection of Minors prohibits selling tobacco, alcohol and lottery tickets to minors and paying out prize money to them, and where age is hard to judge an identity document is checked, which is not the same as retaining an image of the document. Articles 44—45 of the Food Safety Law set out enterprise food safety training and health management; people who come into contact with directly consumed food must obtain an annual health examination certificate, which is not a personal licence for all cashiers.
Boundary of the conclusion

Transaction records are used to trace price versions, payment results, refund bases, shifts and discrepancies; they do not automatically produce legal liability conclusions. Prices and store rules also must not exclude consumers' statutory rights, and refunds, investigations and accounting adjustments are handled by the positions that actually have authority.

Before starting work, check at least six items: the job duties (whether it leans toward pure checkout and settlement, customer service and returns, night or solo shifts, or a store with fresh food, weighing and age-restricted goods), whether you carry responsibility for the till and shift reconciliation and how reconciliation discrepancies are handled, the authorized scope and approval process for refunds, discounts and reversals, the shift pattern and working-time form (fixed shift, rotating shift or peak-hour part-time) and arrangements for standing time, training on and the fault reporting path for checkout equipment, payment terminals and weighing equipment, and the pay method (hourly, or hourly plus commission) together with assessment and responsibility for discrepancies.
Occupational framing

O*NET-SOC 41-2011.00 (SOC 41-2011, cashiers within the sales and related major group), listed as Job Zone 1-2 (little or no preparation to some preparation, SVP below 6.0), and the occupation page marks Bright Outlook; the interest code is CE (Conventional 87, Enterprising 44), and the specific interest areas corresponding to Conventional are led by sales (30), personal service (28), accounting (23) and office work (14); the O*NET industry distribution shows 82% of this occupation in retail trade, 11% in accommodation and food services and 7% in other industries. The official U.S. scope of 41-2011.00 is to receive and pay out money in non-financial establishment settings, possibly using electronic scanning equipment and cash registers or related equipment, and possibly processing credit card and debit card transactions and verifying cheques. The 2022 edition of China's occupational classification code lists cashiers as 4-01-02-04, with work covering cash and cheques, bank cards and mobile payments, consumer vouchers, revenue accounting and discrepancy reporting, and product scanning and handover together with discount and return authorization procedures. The duties overlap with the U.S. SOC41-2011 but the scope must still be checked position by position, and the same name cannot be used to infer that the two countries' statistics and authority are completely equivalent.
Education and training path

BLS SOC41-2011 gives a typical entry of no formal educational credential, no related experience and short-term on-the-job training; OOH notes that employers may prefer a high school diploma or equivalent, and that learning equipment from experienced workers may last up to a few weeks. The general preparation description for O*NET Job Zone1—2 is not the same as a uniform threshold for this occupation; 44%/37%/9% are respondents' judgments about the education new hires need, not the educational attainment of incumbents. No certification was found in the national certification directory at present; the apprenticeship field on the detail page only provides a discovery entry and lists no specific occupation titles, which does not prove that no program or personal licence exists. Chinese education, recruitment and specific position training requirements must be checked against the target store, and no uniform junior or senior high school threshold is set.
Methods and tools

The detail page lists 8 software skill categories, and Hot Technologies lists 6 additional specific technologies: Safari, Firefox and Edge at 2% each, and Excel, Office and Windows at below 1% each (Lightcast2025 U.S. national job postings); categories and item counts, frequency and deployment or personal thresholds are kept separate. On site there are still cash registers, scanners, payment terminals, weighing equipment, cash drawers and voucher equipment, and training follows the actual configuration.
Safety and work permits

The work is mainly standing work and interpersonal contact on the store floor. The O*NET work context shows: 96% are in contact with others continuously; 79% have face-to-face discussions every day; 78% have telephone conversations every day; 67% make decisions every day; 51% stand continuously or almost continuously; 68% work indoors in a controlled environment every day; 46% continuously handle and control objects and tools by hand; 25% consider precision or accuracy extremely important and 46% very important; 27% consider repeating the same tasks extremely important and 26% very important; 12% have a lot of freedom in how they make decisions, 31% some freedom and 50% limited freedom; 34% have very high responsibility for the work results of others; 26% deal with unpleasant, angry or discourteous people every day and 58% at least once a week; 21% experience conflict situations at least once a week; 13% face time pressure every day; 49% say the work is not automated at all; 28% consider the consequences of error serious, 14% fairly serious and 51% not serious at all. The work must follow institutional safety and cash management rules and equipment instructions, and night or solo shifts, cash handling and holding must comply with the institution's loss prevention and personal safety procedures.
Training and regulatory requirements

The U.S. FDA Tobacco21 rule provides that tobacco must not be sold to anyone under 21, and since 2024-09-30 purchasers under 30 of cigarettes, smokeless tobacco and covered tobacco products must have their age verified with photo identification; this is not only a state and local rule. Alcohol, food positions and other local licensing conditions were not checked state by state this round, and institutional training does not automatically create a licence. Article 24 of China's Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests concerns returns, exchanges and repairs for quality non-conformity, while the seven-day no-reason return in Article 25 applies to online, television, telephone and mail-order sales and has exceptions, and is not applied uniformly to all in-store transactions; store rules must not exclude statutory rights. Article 59 of the Law on the Protection of Minors prohibits selling tobacco, alcohol and lottery tickets to minors and paying out prize money to them, and where age is hard to judge an identity document is checked, which is not the same as retaining an image of the document. Articles 44—45 of the Food Safety Law set out enterprise food safety training and health management; people who come into contact with directly consumed food must obtain an annual health examination certificate, which is not a personal licence for all cashiers. Articles 6, 13 and 19 of China's Personal Information Protection Law require clear purposes, minimum necessity, a lawful basis for processing and the shortest necessary retention; financial accounts are sensitive information under Article 28 and require a specific purpose, full necessity and strict protection. Internal store authorization cannot replace a lawful basis on its own; age verification alone does not automatically permit copying the identity document, and transaction vouchers are retained in accordance with laws and regulations rather than being judged as never recordable.
Pay and working hours

OOH notes early and late shifts, weekends, holidays and some night shifts, with part-time work common; the O*NET figures of 51% standing, 13% facing time pressure every day, 26% unpleasant interactions every day and 49% not automated at all are job context, not AI adoption rates. 2025 U.S. national annual wages at P10/P25/P50/P75/P90 were 24,530/28,720/32,880/36,330/40,410 USD, with hourly wages of 11.79/13.81/15.81/17.47/19.43 USD; percentiles are not starting pay, seniority or an individual's take-home income, and the annual value does not reflect an individual's part-time hours. BLS SOC41-2011: employment was 3,106,300 in 2025 and is projected to be 2,905,700 in 2035, a net change of -200,600, or a change rate of -6.5%, with about 521,300 openings per year on average over 2025—2035; the self-employed share was 0.4% in 2025. OOH rounds this to a decline of 6% and states that the openings all come from replacement demand such as workers transferring out or exiting the labour force, not from net new additions or a generative AI attribution. National Bureau of Statistics 2025 average annual wages for wholesale and retail trade: 135,749 CNY for non-private units and 69,622 CNY for private units; accommodation and food services: 62,461 CNY for non-private units and 55,123 CNY for private units (pre-tax). These are all-position references for urban unit industries, not cashier wages, starting pay or wage upper and lower limits. Compare opportunities based on working hours, allowances, discrepancy investigation and actual authority.

Cashiers (O*NET-SOC 41-2011.00, Cashiers) receive and pay out money in non-financial establishment settings, possibly using electronic scanning equipment, cash registers or related equipment, and possibly processing credit card and debit card transactions and verifying cheques. Daily work includes: receiving payments by cash, cheque, credit card, voucher or automatic debit; greeting customers entering the establishment; issuing receipts and handling refunds, points and change owed; assisting customers by providing information and resolving complaints; monitoring the checkout to ensure there is enough cash and adequate staffing; using calculators and cash registers to determine prices of goods, services and admissions and to total bills; answering incoming calls; answering customers' questions about processes and policies; using a paging system to request information or assistance; helping customers find where items are; processing merchandise returns and exchanges; keeping the checkout area clean and orderly and performing general cleaning duties such as mopping and emptying bins; calculating the total amount received in a given period and checking it against total sales; counting the cash in the drawer at the start of the shift to ensure the amount is correct and there is enough change; issuing and redeeming vouchers and coupons; charging expenses to customer or patient accounts; calculating and recording the total transaction amount; weighing and pricing items sold by weight; sorting, counting and bundling cash and coins; periodically preparing balance sheets of transaction amounts and counts; preparing and maintaining non-monetary reports and records; supervising others and providing on-the-job training; assisting in other areas of the store; selling tickets and other goods to customers; stocking shelves and organizing returns and marking prices; bagging, crating, packing and gift-wrapping and preparing parcels for shipping; cashing cheques for customers; and providing carry-out assistance to customers after the transaction. It carries responsibility for pricing, receiving payment, giving change, vouchers, reconciliation and recording, but does not replace the determination of pricing and promotions, refund authority and discrepancy handling by operator, finance and compliance positions.

O*NET occupational identity and tasks: O*NET-SOC 41-2011.00 Cashiers, page updated in 2026, listed as Job Zone 1-2 (little or no preparation to some preparation, SVP below 6.0), and the occupation page marks Bright Outlook. The official duties are 'Receive and disburse money in establishments other than financial institutions. May use electronic scanners, cash registers, or related equipment. May process credit or debit card transactions and validate checks.'; the page lists 28 tasks, of which 12 are core tasks, covering receiving payments by cash, cheque, credit card, voucher or automatic debit (94), greeting customers entering the establishment (93), issuing receipts and handling refunds, points and change (92), assisting customers by providing information and resolving complaints (88), monitoring the checkout to ensure adequate cash and staffing (87), using calculators and cash registers to determine prices and total bills (86), answering incoming calls (85), answering customers' questions about processes and policies (85), using a paging system to request information or assistance (82), helping customers find where items are (82), processing merchandise returns and exchanges (76) and keeping the checkout area tidy and performing cleaning duties such as mopping and emptying bins (75); the rest are supplemental tasks, including calculating the total amount received in a period against total sales (92), counting the cash in the drawer at the start of the shift to ensure the correct amount and enough change (90), issuing and redeeming vouchers and coupons (88), charging expenses to customer or patient accounts (85), calculating and recording the total transaction amount (85), weighing and pricing items sold by weight (85), sorting, counting and bundling cash and coins (85), periodically preparing balance sheets of transaction amounts and counts (84), preparing and maintaining non-monetary reports and records (82), supervising others and providing on-the-job training (81), assisting in other areas of the store (80), selling tickets and other goods (80), stocking shelves and organizing returns and marking prices (79), bagging, crating, packing and gift-wrapping and preparing parcels for shipping (79), cashing cheques for customers (78) and providing carry-out assistance after the transaction (74).

U.S. wages (BLS May 2025 OEWS framing, as shown on this occupation page): the hourly median is 15.81 USD and the annual median is 32,880 USD; the hourly 10th, 25th, 75th and 90th percentiles are 11.79, 13.81, 17.47 and 19.43 USD, and the annual 10th, 25th, 75th and 90th percentiles are 24,530, 28,720, 36,330 and 40,410 USD. The median means half of workers earn above and half below that value; it is not entry-level pay or a starting-pay promise; this occupation is usually trained mainly on the job, and wage percentiles do not represent an individual's job offer.

The 2022 edition of China's occupational classification code lists cashiers as 4-01-02-04, with work covering cash and cheques, bank cards and mobile payments, consumer vouchers, revenue accounting and discrepancy reporting, and product scanning and handover together with discount and return authorization procedures. The duties overlap with the U.S. SOC41-2011 but the scope must still be checked position by position, and the same name cannot be used to infer that the two countries' statistics and authority are completely equivalent. National Bureau of Statistics 2025 average annual wages for wholesale and retail trade: 135,749 CNY for non-private units and 69,622 CNY for private units; accommodation and food services: 62,461 CNY for non-private units and 55,123 CNY for private units (pre-tax). These are all-position references for urban unit industries, not cashier wages, starting pay or wage upper and lower limits. A precise national occupational percentile, starting pay and regional monthly wage were not obtained this round, and industry figures are not filled in as occupational wages.

Work activities are led by getting information (80), performing for or working directly with the public (76), establishing and maintaining interpersonal relationships (53), communicating with people outside the organization (51) and communicating with supervisors, peers or subordinates (51); basic skills are led by active listening and speaking (50 each), critical thinking and reading comprehension (44 each) and mathematics and monitoring (41 each), with writing 28 and science 6; transferable skills are led by service orientation (53), social perceptiveness (50), coordination (44) and time management (41); knowledge is led by customer and personal service (76), English language (59), sales and marketing (52), administration and management (47), mathematics (47) and clerical (46); the interest code is CE (Conventional, Enterprising); work styles are led by dependability (77), integrity (69), social orientation (66) and attention to detail and cooperation (64 each).

paragraphs: This page compares cashiers with six adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference is better suited to. The adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupational descriptions and do not mean that position titles or refund and discount authority and discrepancy determination responsibility can be exchanged.

Evidence note: occupational directions and core outputs are based on O*NET-SOC 41-2011.00 and the official descriptions of the adjacent entries (U.S. framing); the adjacent occupations listed by this evidence route are pharmacy assistants, first-line supervisors of retail sales workers, first-line supervisors of non-retail sales workers, gambling change booth cashiers and counter and rental clerks, while retail salespersons, customer service representatives, bank tellers and stockers and order fillers are same-chain directions among the O*NET related occupations; work scope and refund and discount authority, cash and voucher management, age-restricted purchase limits and customer information protection must be verified separately under each jurisdiction and institution and contract; this page does not present any direction as a shortcut to a career change.

The table below compares how cashiers and the adjacent directions differ in duties and outputs; the basis for judgment is the main outputs, the object of responsibility and the authorization required, not how similar the position titles are.

This direction specialises in rental business, deposits and returns, and receipt and payment is only one part of the business; this occupation centres on receiving payment, giving change, vouchers and reconciliation for retail merchandise transactions, and the merchandise does not involve return or loss determination.

If you would rather do rental business and contract and return management, look first at counter and rental clerks; if you would rather do receiving payment and reconciliation for store transactions, look first at this occupation.
Handling counter rental and service business, processing deposits and returns and extensions and damage, with outputs of rental contracts and deposit and return records.
Counter and rental clerks

Retail salespersons specialise in merchandise promotion, customer relationships and sales performance, and checkout is only one part of it; this occupation centres on accurate amounts and traceable vouchers and reconciliation for transaction settlement.

If you would rather do merchandise promotion, customer development and hitting targets, look first at retail salespersons; if you would rather do transaction settlement and reconciliation and exception handling, look first at this occupation.
Actively promoting merchandise and serving customers and closing sales, with outputs of sales and sales records and customer relationships.
Retail salespersons

Customer service representatives specialise in receiving, tracking and resolving issues and usually do not handle cash or payment settlement; this occupation handles settlement, refunds and vouchers on the store floor at the same time, and the two have different objects of responsibility.

If you would rather do issue intake, tracking and cross-department coordination, look first at customer service representatives; if you would rather do on-site receipt and payment, vouchers and reconciliation, look first at this occupation.
Receiving customer enquiries and complaints and tracking resolution, with outputs of tickets and service and satisfaction records.

paragraphs: Boundary: this section describes occupational risk and work responsibility boundaries, not an evaluation of individuals or institutions; specific procedures and handling processes are determined by the applicable jurisdiction, the institution's price and refund and discount rules, its cash, voucher and till management system, and its store safety and loss prevention requirements.

Direct answer: the main risks include wrong charges and a mismatch between books and stock caused by errors in checking prices, promotions and tax amounts or by deviations in change and refund amounts; shortages and losses caused by poor till, cash and voucher management; financial and compliance losses caused by out-of-scope refunds, discounts and reversals or by assisting fraud; compliance risk from inadequate verification of age-restricted purchases and food, weighing and premises hygiene; privacy and compliance consequences from mishandling customer identity and payment information; and personal safety and loss prevention risks from customer dissatisfaction, conflict and night shifts; controls depend on checking transaction by transaction with documented vouchers, till and reconciliation rules and discrepancy reporting, the authorized scope and exception approval for refunds and discounts, execution of verification, hygiene and food safety requirements, and a clear stop, escalation and loss prevention path.

Tasks and context are checked against O*NET, while risk consequences and controls are editorial analysis, and context percentages are not accident rates. For China, check Articles 24—29 of the consumer law, Articles 6/13/19/28 of the personal information protection law, Article 59 of the minors law and Articles 44—45 of the food law, and for U.S. tobacco check the FDA; the specific payment, discrepancy and night shift rules must still be checked against the actual store.
Cashiers themselves and the shift reconciliation step

Errors in checking prices, promotions and tax amounts or deviations in change and refund amounts cause wrong charges, a mismatch between books and stock and customer disputes (25% consider precision or accuracy extremely important and 46% very important; 28% consider the consequences of error serious).

Check price tags, promotion rules and payment results transaction by transaction; double-check the amount and authority before processing refunds and discounts; consult the shift lead or supervisor about prices and policies that cannot be confirmed; deviations must be recorded and reported, and the books must not be balanced on your own.
Taking and giving change from impression to shorten queues, or skipping promotion and member price checks and settling directly when customers are pressing.
Cashiers themselves and the cash and till management step

Poor till, cash or voucher management may lead to shortages, losses or a mismatch between books and stock; this is a task risk analysis, and the 51% standing figure does not prove how often cash is handed over or how often shortages occur.

Count and hand over the till according to the rules and keep count records; store and manage the drawer and till under institutional rules and limits; follow the store's loss prevention and personal safety procedures when handling and holding cash; discrepancies must be reported immediately with an account of what happened.
Explaining verbally at shift handover without counting, or mixing the till with sales takings and writing the record afterwards.
Cashiers themselves and the refund and discount authorization step

Refunds, discounts, reversals or suspicious requests beyond one's authority may cause losses; exception approval and discrepancy handling are allocated by the actual store's authority, and it is not specified uniformly that every store has a supervisor or finance to approve independently.

Handle refunds, discounts and reversals only within the authorized scope; when beyond that authority or when circumstances are suspicious, stop first and ask the shift lead or supervisor to deal with it; refund vouchers, reasons and the approving person must be fully documented; suspected fraud or collusion must be reported under the rules.

Refunding beyond your authority to keep a customer relationship, or making an exception without checking the transaction basis and applicable rules; it cannot be required that all returns must be accompanied by an identity document.
Cashiers themselves and the compliance verification step

Failure to meet requirements on age-restricted sales, food tasks and weighing may create consumer and safety risks; the specific conditions are checked against the product sold, the jurisdiction and your own tasks.

Article 24 of China's Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests concerns returns, exchanges and repairs for quality non-conformity, while the seven-day no-reason return in Article 25 applies to online, television, telephone and mail-order sales and has exceptions, and is not applied uniformly to all in-store transactions; store rules must not exclude statutory rights. Article 59 of the Law on the Protection of Minors prohibits selling tobacco, alcohol and lottery tickets to minors and paying out prize money to them, and where age is hard to judge an identity document is checked, which is not the same as retaining an image of the document. Articles 44—45 of the Food Safety Law set out enterprise food safety training and health management; people who come into contact with directly consumed food must obtain an annual health examination certificate, which is not a personal licence for all cashiers. The U.S. FDA Tobacco21 rule provides that tobacco must not be sold to anyone under 21, and since 2024-09-30 purchasers under 30 of cigarettes, smokeless tobacco and covered tobacco products must have their age verified with photo identification; this is not only a state and local rule. Alcohol, food positions and other local licensing conditions were not checked state by state this round, and institutional training does not automatically create a licence. Record the necessary verification results and do not photograph identity documents by default; when anomalies are found, pause the relevant sales you are handling and report.
Omitting age verification in order to complete a sale, or settling out-of-date goods or goods with abnormal labels as if they were normal.
Cashiers themselves and the customer information protection step
Mishandling customer identity information, payment information, membership data and surveillance footage leads to privacy and compliance consequences.

Articles 6, 13 and 19 of China's Personal Information Protection Law require clear purposes, minimum necessity, a lawful basis for processing and the shortest necessary retention; financial accounts are sensitive information under Article 28 and require a specific purpose, full necessity and strict protection. Internal store authorization cannot replace a lawful basis on its own; age verification alone does not automatically permit copying the identity document, and transaction vouchers are retained in accordance with laws and regulations rather than being judged as never recordable. Staff must not leak, sell or unlawfully provide customer data, must not pass sensitive data into unapproved tools, and must report anomalies through the store process.
Photographing or forwarding receipts or images of identity documents containing customer information, or repeating a customer's payment information in public.
Cashiers themselves and the store safety step

Customer dissatisfaction, conflict and night shifts bring personal safety and loss prevention risks (26% deal with unpleasant, angry or discourteous people every day and 58% more than once a week; 21% experience conflict situations more than once a week).

Handle complaints and conflict through institutional procedures and call the shift lead or security staff promptly; follow the institution's procedures on cash holding, access control and alarms during night and solo shifts; in situations that threaten personal safety, put your own safety first and call the police and report immediately.
Arguing with a customer who is emotionally agitated or handling a dispute alone in an area without surveillance, or leaving the store alone with cash at night.

entries.answer: Receive and pay out money in non-financial establishment settings, possibly using electronic scanning equipment and cash registers or related equipment, and possibly processing credit card and debit card transactions and verifying cheques: receiving payment by cash, cheque, credit card, voucher or automatic debit and greeting customers; issuing receipts and handling refunds, points and change owed; assisting customers by providing information and resolving complaints; monitoring the checkout to ensure adequate cash and staffing; using calculators and cash registers to determine prices of goods, services and admissions and to total bills; answering incoming calls and answering customers' questions about processes and policies; using a paging system to request assistance; helping customers find where items are; processing merchandise returns and exchanges; keeping the checkout area tidy and performing cleaning duties such as mopping and emptying bins; calculating the total amount received in a given period and checking it against total sales; counting the cash in the drawer at the start of the shift to ensure the correct amount and enough change; issuing and redeeming vouchers and coupons; charging expenses to customer or patient accounts; calculating and recording the total transaction amount; weighing and pricing items sold by weight; sorting, counting and bundling cash and coins; periodically preparing balance sheets of transaction amounts and counts; preparing and maintaining non-monetary reports and records; supervising others and providing on-the-job training; assisting in other areas of the store; selling tickets and other goods; stocking shelves and organizing returns and marking prices; bagging, packing and preparing parcels for shipping; cashing cheques for customers; and providing carry-out assistance.
entries.question: What do cashiers do every day?

entries.answer: The main risks include wrong charges and a mismatch between books and stock caused by errors in checking prices, promotions and tax amounts or by deviations in change and refund amounts; shortages and losses caused by poor till, cash and voucher management; financial and compliance losses caused by out-of-scope refunds, discounts and reversals or by assisting fraud; compliance risk from inadequate verification of age-restricted purchases and food, weighing and premises hygiene; privacy and compliance consequences from mishandling customer identity and payment information; and personal safety and loss prevention risks from customer dissatisfaction, conflict and night shifts; controls depend on checking transaction by transaction with documented vouchers, till and reconciliation rules and discrepancy reporting, the authorized scope and exception approval for refunds and discounts, execution of verification and hygiene requirements, and a clear stop, escalation and loss prevention path.
entries.question: What risks should I pay attention to in advance in this job?

entries.answer: The fit signals are being able to keep pricing and change accurate under continuous customer flow and long periods of standing, being willing to check prices, promotions and payment results transaction by transaction, being able to handle and escalate through the process when a customer is dissatisfied or equipment fails, and being willing to reconcile cash and transaction discrepancies at shift handover and report them truthfully; the key is whether you have reviewable payment, change and voucher records, shift reconciliation and discrepancy records, and return, exchange and complaint handling records, rather than only having helped out at a convenience store or a piece of store experience.
entries.question: How do I judge whether this job suits me?

entries.answer: Candidate item recognition and pricing prompts, calculating change and totalling transactions, organizing reconciliation sheets and discrepancy lists, and drafting return and complaint tickets can all be assisted; physical identification and weighing and pricing double-checks, refund and discount authorization, age and identity verification, customer dispute handling and discrepancy determination are still checked and owned by authorized personnel.
entries.question: Which steps will AI and automation change?

entries.answer: Whether the physical goods and packaging match the scan result, the actual readings of weighing and pricing, the actual verification of customer identity and age-restricted goods, whether refunds and discounts are within the authorized scope, discrepancies between physical cash and vouchers and the books, and judgments about compliance and customer information handling must all be completed and documented by authorized or qualified people.
entries.question: Which steps must keep human checks?

entries.answer: Mainly on-site store work and standing work, with intensity fluctuating around peak customer flow, holidays and night shifts; the work context shows 51% stand continuously or almost continuously, 13% face time pressure every day, 12% have a lot of freedom in how they make decisions, 31% some freedom and 50% limited freedom, and 34% have very high responsibility for the work results of others; the working style is built around counting the till, pricing, receiving payment and giving change, issuing vouchers, handling returns, exchanges and complaints, and shift reconciliation and handover.

subject.name: Cashiers
subject.summary: This page entry corresponds to cashiers (O*NET-SOC 41-2011.00, Cashiers): receiving and paying out money in non-financial establishment settings, possibly using electronic scanning equipment and cash registers or related equipment, and possibly processing credit card and debit card transactions and verifying cheques — receiving payment by cash, cheque, bank card, mobile payment and vouchers, checking items, prices, promotions and tax amounts, issuing receipts and handling refunds and change, counting the till and checking the transaction and total sales amounts and preparing reports, handling returns, exchanges and complaints and escalating according to authority, and keeping the checkout area tidy and restocked; the work is mainly standing on the store floor and interpersonal contact (96% are in contact with others continuously, 79% have face-to-face discussions every day, 51% stand continuously or almost continuously, 26% deal with unpleasant, angry or discourteous people every day, 49% say the work is not automated at all), and its duties do not replace the determination of refunds, discrepancies and compliance matters by operator, finance and compliance positions; the occupation page marks Bright Outlook.
